clues:
Topic 1: Impact of the pandemic on service delivery (referral practices, operational changes)  
- “We refer them for further treatment. We don’t have treatment for such patients here.”  
- “We stop all in coming patients at the steps and ask them to put on their face masks.”  
- “We put a hold on deliveries because of the night curfew. … We advise them to go to the government hospital.”  
- “We have returned to our normal routine.”  

Topic 2: Patient access and behavior changes due to fear and curfew  
- “Patients were coming. To say that because of the Corona they were afraid to come, least they catch the sick, no they were coming.”  
- “Some were afraid. They say: ‘I wouldn’t dare to give birth at that hospital, least the say I have Corona’”  
- “Fear of the curfew, we just advice them to go to the government hospital.”  

Topic 3: Supply chain and financial challenges (drug shortages, cost increases)  
- “Drugs we use to buy at Le 2000, we now buy them at Le 5000. For example, we used to buy novalgin at Le. 1000 for 10 tablets, now cost us Le. 5000.”  
- “We experienced that because, not all the drugs supplies we used to receive before the Corona were included in our supplies after the outbreak.”  

Topic 4: Legacy of the Ebola outbreak influencing response strategies  
- “The only change is the face mask. Because, as for the hand washing, it has been part of us since the Ebola outbreak.”  
- “The government tried. All entry points into our country were blocked. … They stop all international traveling.”  

Topic 5: Mental health and lack of support for healthcare workers  
- “We were stressed because we were afraid as we come to work. … possibility of been infected through a patient one might be attending to and then go home to our families with the sick.”  
- “Was any support provided for you, to deal with these changes? Respondent: No.”  

Topic 6: Staff shortages and payment issues affecting service continuity  
- “I have worked here for government for two years without salary.”  
- “Any addition to your staff number as a result of the corona? Respondent: No they did not add any staff.”  

Topic 7: PPE availability and reliance on past outbreak supplies  
- “I didn’t witness any supply of PPEs during this corona, but we have them. … supply since during the Ebola outbreak I think.”  
- “We were only receiving masks.”
reasoning:
Topic 1: The pandemic disrupted service delivery through referrals and operational changes. Quotes about referring patients due to lack of treatment capacity and halting deliveries during curfews indicate altered care pathways. Mask enforcement at entry points and resuming "normal routine" later show adaptive operational measures. These changes reflect strained resources and policy-driven adjustments to prioritize safety.  

Topic 2: Fear and curfew influenced patient behavior ambiguously. While some continued seeking care, others avoided hospitals due to stigma ("afraid the say I have Corona") or curfew constraints, prompting referrals to government hospitals. This mix of resilience and avoidance highlights how fear and policies shaped access.  

Topic 3: Supply chain and financial strain are evident in soaring drug costs (e.g., Novalgin price hikes) and reduced drug availability post-pandemic. These clues directly tie to financial challenges and shortages, forcing providers to adapt to limited resources.  

Topic 4: Ebola’s legacy is seen in pandemic response strategies. Handwashing practices, retained from Ebola, and government border closures mirror past outbreak measures. The reliance on existing protocols (masks as the only new addition) underscores how prior experiences shaped the response.  

Topic 5: Healthcare workers faced mental health stress from infection fears but received no institutional support. The explicit denial of support ("No") links directly to systemic neglect of their well-being during crises.  

Topic 6: Staff shortages and unpaid salaries for years hindered service continuity. No added staff despite rising demand and delayed payments reveal systemic resource gaps undermining service delivery.  

Topic 7: PPE reliance on Ebola-era stock (e.g., "supply since Ebola") and limited new supplies (only masks) highlight insufficient pandemic preparedness, forcing dependence on outdated resources.
